A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Olaf-World/SeqDelta-REPA study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original linear-probing, action-transfer, adaptation, and generalization results, together with design, data-budget, and LoRA-rank ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds reference-encoder sensitivity results in Table 5 and qualitative latent-action interpolation results in Figure 11.

M1.justification: The latent-action model, SeqDelta-REPA objective, world-model conditioning, and adaptation procedure remain unchanged. Alternative reference encoders and interpolated controls are investigated as experimental variants, without revising the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the MiraData categories, MIND first-/third-person control tasks, and 50-initial-frame OOD evaluation set. The added studies vary reference encoders and latent-action strength within the existing coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 5 compares alignment using VideoMAEv2 and DINOv3 against V-JEPA2 and NONE, explicitly identified as AdaWorld. These are newly evaluated reference-encoder variants; the original AdaWorld and DirectAct comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds a reference-encoder comparison using a common 10-epoch schedule and an interpolation/extrapolation protocol with alpha values 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, and 2 under fixed-image, repeated-control conditioning. Existing experimental settings are retained; the shorter schedule applies only to the new sensitivity study.

E4.justification: V2 adds focused analyses of reference-encoder dependence and local latent-space geometry through action interpolation/extrapolation. The data-budget and LoRA-rank sweeps already appeared in v1 Appendix D; their move to Section 4.5.2 adds no new analysis. Existing failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and training curves without independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the adaptation-scaling values are unchanged. New Table 5 reports 10-epoch results, including 1st-to-3rd Macro-F1 of 0.2972 for V-JEPA2, 0.4697 for VideoMAEv2, 0.1782 for DINOv3, and 0.1382 for AdaWorld. Figure 11 adds qualitative evidence of stronger motion with increasing alpha. These supplement the original results under distinct settings.

T1.justification: V2 adds Equation (14), defining interpolated/extrapolated control codes as a linear combination of NO-OP and action prototypes. This is a limited mathematical definition for the new analysis; Appendix A's symmetry proposition, proof, and beta-VAE discussion remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about cross-context non-identifiability, effect-aligned latent actions, zero-shot transfer, and data-efficient adaptation. The added studies support these claims without redefining the headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the encoder comparison as evidence for the importance of temporal representations and applicability across reference backbones. It also interprets interpolation results as suggesting coherent local latent geometry. Existing failure explanations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new sensitivity study's 10-epoch budget and the interpolation coefficients, repeated-latent conditioning, fixed initial image, and displayed timesteps. Appendix B's architecture, optimization, hardware, and training-time information, along with reported project access, remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to VideoMAE V2, DINOv3, Rotstein et al. (2025), and Yu et al. (2020), supporting the new encoder study and existing future-work discussion. The main related-work framing and novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: V2 splits Section 4.5 into latent-action learning and world-model adaptation subsections, moves the adaptation-sweep discussion from the appendix, and renumbers subsequent appendices. It also makes localized wording corrections and adds acknowledgments and conference information.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 5 and interpolation Figure 11, moves Figure 10 into the main text with a revised caption, and renumbers the retained failure-case figure to Figure 12. It also adjusts the teaser animation and page layout, including splitting the abstract across columns.

improvement.justification: Table 5 tests dependence on the reference encoder, while Figure 11 supplies additional evidence about controllable latent-space geometry. These address previously untested questions and modestly strengthen the paper. Their scope remains limited by the short sensitivity-training schedule and qualitative interpolation evaluation; the main results, formal argument, and limitations are unchanged.
